result.title: Controlling Action-Head Co-Adaptation to VLM Representation Anisotropy
result.summary: Modern learning systems increasingly combine pretrained models with downstream heads. Despite the growing importance of such modular designs, how the downstream model co-adapts to the geometry of pretrained representations remains relatively underexplored. We study this problem through vision-language-action models (VLAs), where a pretrained vision-language model (VLM) conditions an action model for control. We find that the action model progressively concentrates its sensitivity on high-variance dimensions of the VLM outputs. Through controlled experiments across different backbone-head models, we further show that counteracting this sensitivity concentration can be beneficial under representation--task mismatch settings. Motivated by these observations, we introduce \emph{Adaptive Interface Equalizer} (AdaIE), a parameter-free mechanism that reweights pretrained representations according to the evolving downstream sensitivity during training. AdaIE improves VLA success rates on simulation benchmarks, with gains of up to $+5.28$ percentage points (pp) on RoboCasa-GR1 and $+1.68$ pp on RoboTwin 2.0, and achieves an average gain of $+19$ pp across five real-world manipulation tasks. It further generalizes to diffusion policies and world models, improving downstream performance in both settings. Our results highlight interface co-adaptation as an important optimization problem when coupling pretrained representations with downstream models.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 VLM 与下游动作头联合适配时出现的表示各向异性问题：发现动作模型会逐步把敏感性集中到 VLM 输出的高方差维度，并提出无参数的 AdaIE，按训练中不断变化的下游敏感性对预训练表示加权，在 VLA 仿真与真机操作任务上取得增益。
AI.relevance_reason: 「表示各向异性 + 下游敏感性集中」可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否被少数高方差维度主导、是否造成信息坍缩，其无参数按使用度重加权机制也可能为 latent 贡献分配或监督提供线索；但研究对象是动作控制而非推理状态，迁移性需自行判断。
